answer_1.quote: We used the ChatGPT model (gpt-3.5-turbo, default parameters) ... to create the comparative answers ... resulting in 336 summaries in total. ... We propose specific criteria for evaluating the quality of comparative summaries, focusing on structural coherence, conciseness, and faithfulness through explicit source citation.
answer_1.outputs: comparative summaries/answers that compare two objects

answer_2.quote: We employ the following evaluation metrics: Jaccard similarity & Levenstein distance... Semantic similarity: we use the SBERT model... Argument Relevance (Precision, Recall, F1)... Argument-Answer Coherence (AAC): we use the GPT-4 model to check whether the citation supports the correct object.

answer_3.quote: Argument-Answer Coherence (AAC): we use the GPT-4 model to check whether the citation supports the correct object, e.g., Argument 3 "Cats are smarter than dogs" cannot be cited in the excerpt "Dogs are smarter than cats [3]".

answer_4.quote: A total of 282 Toloka users ... contributed to the annotation pool. Each sentence was annotated by a minimum of two participants... We engaged four expert annotators to refine and improve 50 selected outputs from the Silver dataset, following the predefined "Summary Criteria".
answer_4.guideline: Summary Criteria checklist used by expert annotators to assess and revise generated summaries.
